R01.title: Colorado State University: Irrigation Scheduling - The Water Balance Approach (reviewed 2025)
R01.scope: Weather accounting can guide irrigation; initial water, storage, crop loss and inputs must be characterized. Occasional reference checks help detect drift.

R02.title: University of Minnesota: Evapotranspiration-based irrigation scheduling or water-balance method
R02.scope: Independent description of input/output accounting and initial soil-water requirements; no universal cannabis coefficient.

R03.title: FAO-56 Chapter 8: ETc under soil water stress conditions
R03.scope: Available water, stress and depletion accounting; root depth and initial depletion matter.

R04.title: FAO-56 Chapter 2: FAO Penman-Monteith equation
R04.scope: Grass reference demand differs from actual crop/system loss.

R05.title: Virginia Tech SPES-749P (2026): Identifying Water Stress in Container-Grown Plants
R05.scope: Root development, canopy, medium and container geometry influence stress. General nursery evidence, not a cannabis dose table.

R06.title: Virginia Tech SPES-750P (2026): Measuring Nursery Plant Water Use in Containers
R06.scope: Controlled paired weights can measure whole-container loss and inform profile calibration.

R07.title: UF/IFAS PP379: Field Guide to Hemp Diseases
R07.scope: Powdery mildew, gray mold and root/seedling disease mechanisms; confirmation requires observation/diagnostics.

R08.title: Pacific Northwest Handbooks (March 2026): Hemp Gray Mold / Botrytis Bud Blight and Stem Canker
R08.scope: Botrytis-favouring conditions and cultural prevention; no general weather-only infection probability.

R09.title: Rutgers Cooperative Extension E374: Emerging Diseases of Hemp in New Jersey
R09.scope: Field leaf-spot and other disease observations; regional findings are not universal diagnostic rules.

R10.title: Cornell Hemp (2024): The role of weather in disease progression
R10.scope: Weather, waterlogging, airflow and disease exposure; wind can also spread pathogens.

R11.title: UF/IFAS MG025: Cold Protection of Landscape Plants
R11.scope: Radiational cooling can produce surface frost distinct from reported air temperature; general landscape evidence.

R12.title: University of Maryland Extension (2026): Growing Vegetables in Containers and Salad Tables
R12.scope: Container materials, wetting, drainage and hot surfaces; general container evidence.

R13.title: OpenWeather One Call API 3.0 documentation
R13.scope: Field semantics, forecast/current separation, UTC times, precipitation and official alerts.

R14.title: Open-Meteo Weather Forecast API documentation
R14.scope: Candidate modelled reference ET/radiation and layer-labelled regional soil data; no on-site pot observation.

R15.title: Duong et al. (2023): Variation in Hydric Response of Two Industrial Hemp Varieties
R15.scope: Cultivar/setup differences in controlled conditions limit transfer of universal coefficients.

R16.title: Gill et al. (2025): Water conservation and assimilation is driven by stomatal behaviour in industrial hemp
R16.scope: Water supply affects gas exchange; weather demand is not a linear actual transpiration meter.

R17.title: FAO-56 Chapter 3: Meteorological data
R17.scope: VPD, radiation, wind-height and reduced-data ET methods and their limitations.

R18.title: Punja et al. (2023): Yeast and mold levels in cannabis inflorescences
R18.scope: Greenhouse floral microclimate differs from ambient; not a fixed outdoor correction.

R19.title: Penn State Extension: Powdery Mildew
R19.scope: Humidity, free-water and dispersal relationships vary among powdery mildews. General context; no cannabis-specific infection threshold.

R20.title: UC IPM (2024): Damping-off Diseases in the Garden
R20.scope: Vulnerable emerging seedlings, root-zone conditions and differences between air and soil temperature. General host evidence.

R21.title: National Weather Service: Dew and Frost Development
R21.scope: Dew-point depression, radiational cooling, cloud and wind context; ambient conditions do not measure a leaf surface.

R22.title: University of Minnesota Extension (2026): Keep gardens thriving through the heat
R22.scope: Heat-related wilt can occur despite adequate soil water. General garden evidence; no universal cannabis injury temperature.

R23.title: National Weather Service: Understanding Wind Chill
R23.scope: Human wind-chill index definition and skin-oriented assumptions; not a plant temperature model.

R24.title: NOAA JetStream: Thunderstorm Hazards - Hail
R24.scope: Hail is a storm process; do not infer it from surface RH, rain chance or surface freezing temperature.

R25.title: Oregon State University Horticulture: Disease Triangle
R25.scope: Disease requires a susceptible host, suitable pathogen and environment. Unobserved pathogen presence limits weather-only disease claims.

R26.title: UC IPM archived research model: Botrytis Bunch Rot of Grape
R26.scope: Example of fitted temperature/wetness interactions and crop/location validation. Archived grape models are not cannabis weights, thresholds or recommendations.

warnings.missingBehavior: No usable root evidence -> no present aeration/pathogen assertion. A symptom-only branch stays explicitly cause_unknown.
warnings.output: Possible root-environment problem or reported symptoms: investigate drainage/current roots and keep the cause unconfirmed.
warnings.claimLimits: Environmental conditions, symptoms and confirmed disease are different claims. Heat alone can cause wilt even with adequate water. [R22] Root-disease organisms do not share one universal weather threshold.
acceptanceCases: needsWater=false alone does not qualify.
W07 and W14 merge into one root card with preserved reasons.
Wilt without root evidence yields cause_unknown, not automatic drought or root rot.
warnings.triggerInputMeaning: Alternative branches as stated in predicate; this flat list is not an all-fields-required gate.

Environmental route is W07, never a second weather score.
formalLogic.primary: W07 evidence OR a current qualified symptom report, with different claims.
formalLogic.secondary: Scoped root temperature/EC/pH and actual injury can support differential review.
formalLogic.context: Prior needsWater=false, regional RH and weather cannot supply a root diagnosis.
formalLogic.interaction: Wilt can have different causes. A symptom route does not establish excess water; a root-excess route does not identify a pathogen.
formalLogic.related: One W07/W14 card with retained child reasons; W13 is tissue-specific context.
